overhead_breakdown_run3.preflight_steps: route 1s, repo rev 2s, binaries 4s, remote dirs 2s, sd-cli --help + model stat 4s (sequential ssh round trips)
overhead_breakdown_run3.remote_generation_note: sd-cli generate_image 14.85s + process start/mmap/remote write + copy back

findings: Per-run weight reload is cheap here: logged tensor loads total ~1.1-1.3 s per run (sd15, OS file cache warm after run 1; cold run 1 was not slower), so a resident sd-server would save little on sd15 at this size.

The dominant avoidable cost is preflight: ~14 s of sequential ssh checks per job (about 37% of wall time). Collapsing them into one ssh call is a candidate optimisation; NOT implemented (worker-script change, out of scope).

Cold vs warm difference is within noise (38.57 s vs 37.56-38.67 s): the model was already in the Big Mac page cache from the A/B runs, so this is a warm-cache "cold" start. A true cold start (after page-cache eviction or reboot) is UNVERIFIED.
